verdict.rationale: Elicit's first-party docs describe several sharing paths. Analysts can invite team members into live Research Agent sessions, where collaborators with edit access can ask questions, create artifacts and edit artifacts. Workflows can be shared via a view-only link that works without an account, and collections can be shared with colleagues. Shared items arrive in the recipient's Recents. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the sharing and collaboration features.

support.subject: As an analyst, I can share a research session or report with collaborators who can view or build on it

citations.quote: Invite your team members to collaborate live with you in Research Agent sessions.
Collaborators with edit access can ask the agent questions in your session, produce new artifacts (documents, tables, etc.), and edit other artifacts
Toggle on "Anyone with the link can view", then click "Copy link". This works for people without an Elicit account
Recents is also where anything shared with you arrives.
